title: Per-direction IO Crediting & Streaming Grace Tier — experiment proposal
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Background: Customers increasingly surface large resends of prompts (system + user) plus long streaming responses. Current uniform per-token pricing conflates ingress (input) and egress (output) cost profiles and disincentivizes streaming-heavy UX for enterprise customers. We need an experiment that tests asymmetric per-token crediting with a short streaming "grace" buffer to evaluate economic and UX impacts, while keeping contract simplicity for enterprise security questionnaires.

Objectives: 1) Measure whether separating billed input vs output tokens (directional rates) plus a small streaming "grace" buffer (first 4 tokens free per stream event for low-latency UX) reduces observed cost pressure on customers and increases streaming adoption. 2) Quantify unit economics impact to Redwood (net RPM), forecast revenue under enterprise commits, and identify fraud/abuse signals. 3) Validate enterprise contract language and security questionnaire updates needed for per-direction billing.

Hypothesis: Directional rates with a small streaming grace will make streaming integrations 15–30% cheaper for chat-heavy customers without materially decreasing Redwood's revenue for top deciles; this will increase streaming-enabled feature adoption by 10–20% in pilot cohort.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Primary: delta in streaming-enabled request share for pilot customers (+ target +10%).
- Revenue: net change in ARPA for pilot cohort (accept +/- 5% variance).
- Cost: measured change in per-token cost to Redwood (GPU cost + infra) for pilot cohort (no more than +3% for overall).
- Abuse signal: % of requests flagged for abnormal token churn (threshold >5% change triggers rollback).

Design & experiment plan:
- Variant A (Control): current symmetric per-token pricing.
- Variant B (Directional): input token rate = 0.6x base, output token rate = 1.4x base (preserves weighted avg for baseline traffic mix).
- Variant C (Directional + Grace): same as B but each streaming session gets a 4-token grace window per stream event where outputs are not charged (streaming metadata marks events).
- Pilot population: 40 mid-size customers (randomized), prioritized by chat-heavy usage and engaged account teams. 10% traffic sample for each pilot customer, ramp to 100% over 3 weeks.
- Duration: 6 weeks active + 1 week analysis.
- Measurement: token-metering logs, cost model integration (ENG), per-customer dashboards (console-calcs).

Pricing examples (illustrative):
- Baseline price: $0.02 / 1k tokens (symmetric).
- Variant B: input = $0.012 / 1k, output = $0.028 / 1k. For a 20/80 input/output split, effective price = $0.0248 / 1k (slight increase).
- Variant C with streaming grace: short bursts (10-token long outputs) get first 4 tokens free reducing effective output cost for streaming-heavy patterns by ~40%.

Risks & mitigations:
- Customer confusion: update billing docs, console shows per-direction breakdown, SDKs add directional counters.
- Revenue downside: cap total monthly delta per enterprise customer via grace credit ceilings.
- Abuse: flag streams with >x restarts or repeated tiny responses; ENG to add rate-limiter and anomaly detection.
- Contract complexity: product to draft simple exhibit language for enterprise contracts clarifying directional rates, grace caps, and auditability. Legal review required.

Dependencies: ENG changes to token metering (ENG-5201), Console display work (ENG-6118), billing system support for dual rates (FIN-220), legal & sales alignment on contract exhibit (PM-31789).

Rollout & gating:
- Gate 1 (week 1): internal mirror test + synthetic load to validate metering.
- Gate 2 (week 2–3): 10 pilot customers at 10% traffic. Verify dashboards and fraud signals.
- Gate 3 (week 4–6): ramp to 100% pilot traffic. If revenue delta > -5% or abuse > threshold, pause and iterate.

Required approvals: PM, Pricing committee, Legal (contract exhibit), Security review for metering telemetry (see security_review_required).

Deliverables:
- PRD (this doc + Confluence pages), console UI mocks, billing schema changes, sample enterprise contract exhibit, pilot analysis dashboard.

Next steps: align with ENG on metering timeline (weekly sync), legal to draft exhibit, prepare pilot customer outreach templates, and instrument anomaly detection rules.
